label: The Battle of Actium, as its sources tell it

guidance: In this Life, "Caesar" in the narrative of Antony's war with him denotes Octavian (later Augustus), not Julius Caesar.
In Dio's account of these years, "Caesar" denotes Octavian (later Augustus), not Julius Caesar.
Dio composes speeches for his characters. What a speaker asserts inside a speech is rhetoric Dio gives that speaker, not Dio's narrative: draft nothing from inside a speech.
This is a modern historian's work, not an ancient source. Draft as claims what the author states about the people, forces, places, and events in scope.

Where the author reads an event as an instance of an in-scope concept, draft exemplifies; where the author presents a long-range consequence of it, draft ledTo. Record any other reading of what the events meant as a note of type interpretation.
The in-scope entity Augustus is the person modern authors usually call Octavian before 27 BCE. Decide from context whom the author means by Caesar.
The author's footnotes and any transcriber's notes are not the passage text.

This inquiry is the battle itself, not any one book. Read each source for the steps of the battle as that source tells them: the decisions and movements that lead into it, the fighting, and the flight, pursuit, and surrender that end it, when the source ties them to the battle. Each step is a depicted event of this source.
A fleet, a wing or the centre of a fleet, a squadron, or a land army in scope can take part in a depicted event as a participant, as a person can.
Order the steps only where the source orders them: by a time marker, by saying one followed another, or by presenting one as the cause or outcome of another.

For participatedIn in the battle as a whole, a person counts as taking part when the passage shows them present during it: commanding, fighting, aboard a ship in the action, or fleeing from it. Preparations before the event, or the actions of a person's ships or troops with no sign of the person, do not by themselves show that the person took part.

commanded relates a person to a force they directed in action, using the force entities in scope: a fleet, one wing or the centre of a fleet, a squadron, or a land army. Command of a wing or the centre is not command of the whole fleet; use the most specific force the passage supports.

heldAuthorityOver is formal or supreme authority over a force, whether or not the person directed it in the fighting, for example an overall commander whose subordinate leads a wing. Draft it when the passage shows that authority, with a time only if the passage gives one.

Give a time marker in the source's own words as the time expression. Add time_edtf only when the passage states the year. Notes by a modern editor, translator, or transcriber are never the author's text.
